messages:
sam_garcia: Morning folks, first-week snag. I followed the README but when I run the app locally it times out connecting to Redis. Error is `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`. I have Docker running and the compose stack up.

Tess: Welcome! Quick check: is your app running on the host or inside a container? If host, it needs the redis service to be port-mapped to localhost.

sam_garcia: App is running on host (node dev server). Compose has `ports:\n  - \"6379:6379\"` for redis so I thought it would work. `docker ps` shows redis container running.

owen_r: Two things to check: 1) Is there another redis on host shadowing the port? `lsof -i :6379` 2) On mac, if you used a socket path in REDIS_URL (unix:///tmp/redis.sock) it won't work unless the container binds that socket into host.

sam_garcia: `lsof` returned nothing. I'm also seeing `permission denied` in redis logs around creating `/data/`, but container still says started. Could a failed init cause it not to accept connections?

Tess: Yes, if redis can't write its data dir it might exit or refuse connections. Check `docker-compose logs redis` for the full error. Also ensure your compose uses a named volume or chowned host dir.

owen_r: Another weird one I've seen: if your app config uses `127.0.0.1` but Docker for Mac maps container to a different interface, sometimes connecting to `localhost` fails in odd networking setups. But with port mapping it should be fine.

sam_garcia: Logs show `Creating server TCP listening socket *:6379: Permission denied` which is odd. I used a custom redis image with `USER redis` layer. Maybe that user doesn't have permission on the bind mount.

Tess: Try removing host bind for redis data to see if it starts without the mount: change `- ./redisdata:/data` to a named volume like `- redisdata:/data` under volumes. That will tell if bind mount perms are the culprit.

infra-bot: FYI: onboarding doc "local-services" recommends named volumes for mac: https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services#mac-binding
\nnowen_r: If you need to keep the host dir, run `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ./redisdata` (replace 1000 with the redis uid in your image) then restart.

sam_garcia: I switched to named volume and redis came up fine, app connected. I moved my local fixtures out and will follow the named-volume pattern. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:

Tess: Great! Ping if you want the `scripts/reset-redis.sh` we use to archive host dir before resetting.
